q1.answer: No. ADR013 (use node-fetch) is superseded by ADR014 (proper use of HTTP fetching libraries / native fetch), which says frontend plugins and packages should prefer the injected fetchApiRef rather than importing node-fetch or raw fetch directly — matching how NotificationsClient takes fetchApi via its constructor.
q1.source: docs/architecture-decisions/adr014-use-fetch.md (see also tree card for adr014, which notes it replaces adr013)

q2.answer: ADR007 requires all `fetch`/`XMLHTTPRequest` calls in tests to be mocked via msw instead of each test rolling its own mocking approach. Per the ADR, this avoids the inconsistency of every test having its own ad hoc implementation of request mocking, and avoids having to mock `fetch` itself directly (browser or node).

q3.answer: ADR006 cites that React.FC implicitly adds a `children` prop to every component, and that it does not support generic types on children. As a concrete upstream fact, it notes Facebook removed React.FC from the create-react-app base template.

q4.answer: ADR010 names Moment.js as the library luxon replaces, citing two reasons: Moment.js suffers from large bundle size and mutable-state issues, and separately the Moment.js project itself announced it is being sunset/deprecated and recommends switching to a modern alternative.

q5.answer: ADR004 (Module Export Structure) requires every exported symbol to be traceable through index files down to src/index.ts. It was written specifically to make it easy to answer 'Is the export in this module also exported by the package?' (and similarly 'What is exported from this directory?').

q6.answer: No — under ADR004's rule, a symbol is only public if it's traceable through a chain of index files up to src/index.ts; since there's no src/utils/index.ts re-exporting these files and src/index.ts doesn't mention them either, the chain is broken, so they are NOT part of the public API. The ADR explicitly says no private marker is needed: the absence of a re-export anywhere in the index chain is itself sufficient proof the symbol isn't exported.

q7.answer: ADR011 says x-react exists to hold 'shared widgets, hooks and similar that both the plugin itself (x) and third-party frontend plugins can depend on.' So a -react package is only justified once other, third-party frontend plugins need to consume notifications' components/hooks — today those live only inside plugins/notifications/src and aren't depended on externally, so no x-react package is needed.

q8.answer: The one allowed exception is React.lazy-loaded modules, since React.lazy's dynamic import expects a default export. The ADR's workaround for teams wanting to avoid even that is to keep the named export and wrap it at the import site: `React.lazy(() => import('../path/to/Component').then(m => ({ default: m.Component })))`.

q9.answer: ADR015. Its Consequences section says the new `loader`/`component` option pattern will be applied to the new frontend-system APIs (`@backstage/frontend-*` packages) but explicitly states existing APIs for the old frontend system (`@backstage/core-*` packages, which is what dev/index.tsx uses) will NOT be updated/retrofitted.
